purpose: First frozen BM25 retrieval baseline for Synapse STEM-25. This file pins the protocol only; no harness exists and no retrieval has been run.

dataset.review_log_note: The log changes as review proceeds. Open/closed status in the manifest is a snapshot taken at this hash; regenerate the manifest (and re-freeze) if the log changes.

group_definitions.PRIMARY_ANSWERABLE: eval_track=A_transcript_qa and no open review item. Used for Recall@k and MRR.
group_definitions.PRIMARY_UNANSWERABLE: eval_track=A_transcript_qa_abstention and no open review item. NOT used for Recall/MRR (no gold evidence); separate abstention evaluation.
group_definitions.SENSITIVITY_ANSWERABLE: eval_track=A_transcript_qa with an open review item. Reported separately, never merged into the primary numbers.
group_definitions.SENSITIVITY_UNANSWERABLE: eval_track=A_transcript_qa_abstention with an open review item. Separate abstention sensitivity set.
group_definitions.EXCLUDED: eval_track is B_visually_dependent, A_or_B_pending_review or X_EXCLUDED_PENDING_VIDEO_VERIFICATION.

question_manifest.open_review_item_rule: A question is 'open' if it has an item in review_items.csv whose log rows are not both completed with reviewer+review_date and video-row evidence_supported=yes and proposed_action in {keep_as_is, keep_unanswerable}. Questions with no review item are 'no_review_item' (primary).
question_manifest.caveat: The gold labels are NOT fully verified. Of the 176 PRIMARY questions, only MATH04_Q08 has been checked against the video; the other 175 have not been human-reviewed (machine-drafted and mechanically validated only). "No open review item" does not mean "verified".

text_field.source: dataset/synapse_stem25_reviewed_v1/transcript_segments.jsonl -> field "text" (the dataset field "text_normalized" is NOT used)
text_field.rationale: The product loads raw caption text and cleans it with qa.transcript.clean_text; indexing "text" reproduces that path. "text_normalized" would additionally strip speaker labels and drop 5 more cues (CHEM02, CS01-CS04).

preprocessing.clean_text: html.unescape; remove [music|applause|laughter|silence|noise|inaudible] tags (case-insensitive); remove ">>"; collapse whitespace. Speaker labels such as "PROFESSOR:" are NOT removed.
preprocessing.row_dropping: rows with no usable start or with empty cleaned text are dropped, so later segments shift position
preprocessing.end_rule: end = raw end only if it is after start and not past the next start; otherwise the next segment start; last segment gets +3.0 s
preprocessing.sorting: rows are sorted by start; TranscriptSegment.index is 0-based position AFTER dropping and sorting
preprocessing.segment_index_vs_dataset_id: dataset IDs (LECT_S0001...) are 1-based positions BEFORE dropping. Never convert between them by position.

cue_id_mapping.method: stable key = start time (float equality) of the retained segment -> dataset cue_id; the harness must build this per lecture from the same rows it passes to normalize_segments
cue_id_mapping.rule: Never use array position or segment.index to obtain a cue ID. A chunk (first_index..last_index) is converted to cue IDs by looking up each member segment.start in the per-lecture start->cue_id map.
cue_id_mapping.dropped_gold_cue_policy: Dropped cues cannot be retrieved: remove them from the gold set. If a question has no retrievable gold cue it is reported as unscoreable and excluded from metrics (none in primary/sensitivity at creation).

chunking.actual_behavior: Consecutive retained segments are appended to the current chunk while (segment.end - first_segment.start) <= chunk_seconds AND (running characters + len(segment.text) + 1) <= chunk_max_chars; otherwise a new chunk starts. The first segment of a chunk is always accepted, so a single long segment can exceed either limit. Time uses the normalized (capped) segment end. Chunks are non-overlapping and partition the retained segments of the lecture; the chunk set does not depend on the question.

retrieval.idf: ln(1 + (N - df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5)) per question-term group over chunks of the same lecture
retrieval.query: terms = qa.retrieval.content_terms(qa.retrieval._TIME_TEXT_RE.sub(" ", question_text)); groups = [qa.retrieval.expand_term(t) for t in terms]. Includes stemming, stopword removal, the hand-written synonym groups and the ASR alias 8 -> "ate". Query = question_text only.
retrieval.ranked_list: all chunks of the lecture with score > 0, sorted by score descending
retrieval.tie_break: lower chunk index (earlier in the lecture) first; identical to production because sorted(..., reverse=True) is stable
retrieval.zero_score_chunks: never ranked and never counted as retrieved, even if fewer than k chunks have a positive score
retrieval.search_scope: one lecture per question (the question lecture_id); never across lectures
gates_not_applied: merging of adjacent chunks into S1..Sn blocks
retrieval.select_evidence_not_used: qa.retrieval.select_evidence is NOT used for ranking metrics because it returns merged chronological blocks and applies the gates above.
retrieval.full_transcript_chars_note: Pinned to 0 (EvidenceConfig default) so no whole-transcript shortcut can occur; qa/service.py derives this from ASK_FULL_TRANSCRIPT_MAX_TOKENS in production, which must not be read by the harness.
retrieval.time_and_global_routing: Not applicable: parse_time_reference/is_global_question are not used. Preflight at creation found no primary/sensitivity question that would be diverted and none with an empty term list.
retrieval.private_api_note: Uses underscore-prefixed functions (_group, _rank_groups, _TIME_TEXT_RE); pinned by code hash so a change in them is detected.

relevance.rule: A retrieved chunk is relevant to a question if its cue-ID set contains at least one gold-evidence cue ID of that question.
relevance.gold_cue_set: union of segment_ids over all gold intervals, minus cues dropped by preprocessing

metrics.terminology: DISTINCT GOLD INTERVAL = one entry of gold_evidence.json gold_intervals for the question (a maximal run of consecutive cues; adjacent runs were merged when the dataset was built). A chunk COVERS an interval when the chunk's cue IDs overlap that interval's gold cue IDs (at least one shared cue).
metrics.top_k_rule: top k chunks of the raw ranked list (positive BM25 score only). If fewer than k chunks have a positive score, all of them are used; the list is never padded with zero-score chunks.
metrics.recall_definition: Per answerable question: (number of its distinct gold intervals covered by the top-k chunks) / (number of its distinct gold intervals). Gold intervals whose cues were all dropped by preprocessing are removed from the denominator. The reported value is the mean of the per-question values over the questions of the evaluation set.
metrics.recall_is_not: Interval Recall@k is NOT complete-question evidence recall. A single shared cue covers an interval, so a question can score 1.0 while most of its gold cues are not in the top-k chunks, and it is not a cue-level or text-level recall.
metrics.full_evidence_coverage_definition: Proportion of answerable questions in the set for which EVERY distinct gold interval (after removing intervals with no retrievable cue) is covered by the top-k chunks. "Every interval is covered" means every interval shares at least one cue with some top-k chunk; it does not mean every gold cue was retrieved. For single-interval questions it equals Hit Rate@k.
metrics.hit_rate_definition: Proportion of answerable questions in the set with at least one distinct gold interval covered by the top-k chunks (equivalently, at least one top-k chunk is relevant; equivalently per-question interval recall > 0).
metrics.mrr_definition: Per answerable question: 1 / rank of the first relevant chunk in the raw ranked list if that rank <= 10, else 0 (also 0 when no chunk is relevant). Mean over the questions of the set.
invariants_for_harness_tests: Hit Rate@k >= Full-evidence coverage@k for every k
for single-interval questions Hit Rate@k == Full-evidence coverage@k == interval recall@k
Hit Rate@k, interval Recall@k and Full-evidence coverage@k are non-decreasing in k
MRR@10 >= Hit Rate@1 and MRR@10 <= the share of questions with any relevant chunk in the top 10
relevant chunks never include cues from another lecture

reconciliation.with_dataset_readme_section_9: The README's "Recall@5: share of gold intervals covered by at least one top-5 chunk" and "Hit Rate@5: at least one top-5 chunk is relevant" are the same definitions as above, generalized to k = 1, 3, 5. The README example "MRR cut-off e.g. 20" is superseded: MRR depth is 10 here. The README is in the dataset folder and was not edited.
reconciliation.with_previous_config_version: The earlier recall_definition (intervals with >=1 cue in a top-k chunk, divided by all intervals, dropped-cue intervals excluded) is unchanged in meaning; it is now named Interval Recall@k and its limits are stated. Hit Rate@k and Full-evidence coverage@k are new.
reconciliation.readme_supersession: The configured MRR@10 (mrr_depth = 10) supersedes the illustrative "cut-off at a fixed depth, e.g. 20" in dataset_readme.md section 9. The README was deliberately left unchanged (its SHA-256 is pinned in dataset.file_sha256); where it differs from this file, this file governs the baseline.

not_pinned: paired significance tests for a later BM25-vs-hybrid comparison

They stay on a SEPARATE abstention evaluation track that is NOT defined in this protocol (open decision A1). Raw BM25 ranking must not be used to claim production abstention performance.

verification_statement.summary: The gold labels are NOT fully verified. Of the 176 PRIMARY questions, only MATH04_Q08 has been checked against the video; the other 175 have not been human-reviewed (machine-drafted and mechanically validated only).
verification_statement.sensitivity_set: The 13 SENSITIVITY questions have an open review item and are reported separately, never merged into primary numbers.
verification_statement.required_wording: Results must be described as "against machine-drafted gold labels, 1 of 176 primary questions video-checked", not as results against verified gold.
verification_statement.audit_caveats: Audit caveat codes per question are in the manifest column audit_issue_codes (e.g. long evidence spans, caption gaps inside evidence).

order: 1. Source: dataset field "text" of each caption cue (cue IDs LECT_S0001... are 1-based positions before any dropping).

2. qa.transcript.normalize_segments({start: start_seconds, end: end_seconds, text}) -> qa.transcript.clean_text: html.unescape; remove [music|applause|laughter|silence|noise|inaudible] tags (case-insensitive); replace ">>" with a space; collapse whitespace; strip. Cues with empty cleaned text (or no usable start) are dropped; the rest are sorted by start; end is capped at the next start.
3. Chunking (qa.retrieval._group) groups consecutive retained cues; the chunk text is the member cues' cleaned text.

4. Document tokens: qa.retrieval.tokenize(cue.text) for every member cue, summed per chunk. Stopwords are NOT removed from documents (they count toward chunk length in BM25 length normalization). Cues are tokenized separately, so no token sequence spans a cue boundary.

5. tokenize(): lower-case; remove the contraction suffixes 's 't 'd 'm 're 've 'll (straight or curly apostrophe) when they follow a letter; split with [a-z0-9]+; stem() each token; for tokens with a digit 8 and >=2 letters, also emit the ASR alias stem ("li8" -> "liat").

6. stem(): irregular-form map first; tokens that are digits or have <=3 characters are unchanged; otherwise strip the first matching suffix in the order ies->y, ing, ed, es, s (not "ss") provided >=3 characters remain; then drop a final "e" when the token is longer than 4 characters.

7. Query: question_text only. Time expressions are removed with qa.retrieval._TIME_TEXT_RE; content_terms() lower-cases, removes the contraction suffixes, drops stopwords (qa.retrieval._STOPWORDS as finally defined at import), drops single letters not in _KEEP_SINGLE (digits are kept), stems, and keeps unique terms in order.

8. Each query term becomes a group via qa.retrieval.expand_term (hand-written synonym groups). A group's term frequency in a chunk is the sum over its members; df and idf are computed per group; BM25 uses k1=1.5, b=0.75 over the chunks of the question's lecture.

synonym_groups: choose select selection pick decide decision determine prioritize prioritise prefer choice
order ranking rank priority prioritize prioritise sequence hierarchy precedence
substitute substitution replace replacement plug swap

known_text_artifacts.note: Labels such as "AUDIENCE:" or "ERIC LANDER:" are NOT removed by production clean_text, so they are indexed (e.g. "audience" is not a stopword). [INAUDIBLE] tags ARE removed by production clean_text. Caption errors in the source text are kept (see lecture_manifest.csv caption_quality_notes).
known_text_artifacts.tuning_note: Synonym groups, irregular stems and the 8->ate alias were hand-written for another lecture domain (LIATE); this is the production configuration, not tuned for this dataset.

confidence_interval.resampling: For each of B = 10000 replicates draw n question indices with replacement using rng.randrange(n) called n times in order (n = number of answerable questions in the stratum); the replicate value of a metric is the mean of its per-question values over the drawn questions. All metrics in a stratum use the same B replicates. Re-seed random.Random(20261013) at the start of each (set, stratum) so results do not depend on reporting order.
confidence_interval.interval: nearest-rank percentiles of the sorted replicate values: lower = the ceil(0.025*B) = 250th smallest, upper = the ceil(0.975*B) = 9750th smallest
confidence_interval.applies_to: PRIMARY_ANSWERABLE overall and each stratum with sample_flag OK or SMALL; strata with sample_flag VERY_SMALL get counts and point estimates only (no interval)
confidence_interval.limitation: Resampling treats questions as independent. The questions are grouped in 25 lectures (about 5 per lecture), so question-level intervals can be too narrow; the lecture-clustered bootstrap (secondary_sensitivity_analysis, S1) is the pinned check on this.

small_sample_flags.rule: n < 10 -> VERY_SMALL (no CI); 10 <= n < 30 -> SMALL (CI reported with a warning that it is unstable); n >= 30 -> OK

ci_policy.VERY_SMALL: point estimate and sample size only; NO confidence interval
ci_policy.SMALL: point estimate, sample size and confidence interval, with an instability warning attached
ci_policy.OK: point estimate, sample size and confidence interval

breakdowns.rule: Strata are derived from the dataset; no label is invented. Every breakdown row reports n and its sample_flag. The 13 sensitivity questions get no breakdown.

dimensions.subject: questions.csv field "subject"
dimensions.gold_interval_count: derived from the manifest column n_gold_intervals: "1" versus "2+" (distinguishes Hit Rate from Interval Recall)

not_used.lecture_id: about 5 answerable questions per lecture: every stratum would be VERY_SMALL
not_used.difficulty: confounded with question_category in this dataset (49/50 direct_keyword easy, 47/50 multi_segment hard)
not_used.visual_information_required: only visual=false questions are in the primary set

statistics.primary_interval: The question-level percentile bootstrap (confidence_interval) remains the PRIMARY interval for every reported estimate.

secondary_sensitivity_analysis.status: APPROVED (S1) - documented method; no scoring code exists or is added by this protocol
secondary_sensitivity_analysis.role: SECONDARY sensitivity analysis only. It never replaces or overrides the question-level interval; both are reported side by side and labelled.
secondary_sensitivity_analysis.name: lecture-clustered percentile bootstrap
secondary_sensitivity_analysis.cluster_unit: lecture_id (the lecture a question belongs to)
secondary_sensitivity_analysis.applies_to: PRIMARY_ANSWERABLE, overall, for the headline metrics only. Not computed for strata (clusters would be too few and too small).
secondary_sensitivity_analysis.rng: Python standard library random.Random(seed), re-seeded at the start of the analysis
secondary_sensitivity_analysis.resampling: Let L be the lectures that contain at least one PRIMARY_ANSWERABLE question and G = len(L). For each of B = 10000 replicates draw G lectures with replacement using rng.randrange(G) called G times in order; the replicate pool is every PRIMARY_ANSWERABLE question of each drawn lecture (a lecture drawn twice contributes its questions twice). The replicate value of a metric is the mean of its per-question values over the whole pool (pooled mean, so lectures with more questions weigh more).
secondary_sensitivity_analysis.interval: nearest-rank percentiles of the sorted replicate values: the 250th and 9750th smallest (ceil(0.025*B) and ceil(0.975*B)), as for the primary interval
secondary_sensitivity_analysis.purpose: Checks whether the primary question-level interval is too narrow because questions from the same lecture are correlated. If the clustered interval is materially wider, report that.

abstention.status: NOT_DEFINED - DEFERRED (A1); does not block the raw BM25 ranking baseline; scoring unimplemented and no abstention metric pinned
prohibitions: Do not report raw-BM25 ranking scores or score thresholds as abstention performance.
Do not merge unanswerable questions into the Recall/Hit/MRR sets.
Do not describe a retrieval-gate result as "production abstention rate".

facts_from_code.retrieval_gate: qa.retrieval.select_evidence returns decision "no_evidence" when the question has terms and either no query-term group matches the lecture or the IDF-weighted coverage is below EvidenceConfig.min_coverage (= 0.25); this is the only part of abstention decided by retrieval.
facts_from_code.production_behavior_on_no_evidence: qa/service.py answers STATUS_INSUFFICIENT ("insufficient_context") without calling the LLM; its comment says a keyword miss on a long transcript proves nothing about what the lecture covers.
facts_from_code.llm_decides_after_gate: When the gate passes, the LLM returns the final status. A "not_in_lecture" reply is downgraded to "insufficient_context" unless the whole transcript was supplied (plan.complete). Final abstention therefore needs LLM calls, which are out of scope for this phase.
facts_from_code.short_lecture_bypass: Transcripts up to min(ASK_FULL_TRANSCRIPT_MAX_TOKENS x chars_per_token, evidence budget) characters are sent whole and bypass retrieval. Defaults: 2000 tokens x 3.5 = 7000 characters (an upper bound; the evidence budget can lower it). Lectures at or below that bound (cleaned "text", incl. separators): ['MATH01', 'MATH03', 'MATH04', 'PHYS05', 'BIO02', 'CS02'].

required_decisions.decision: What is the target behavior for an unanswerable question: final status other than "answered" (insufficient_context or not_in_lecture), or specifically not_in_lecture? Production downgrades not_in_lecture to insufficient_context unless the whole transcript is supplied.

Is a retrieval-gate-only diagnostic (gate "no_evidence" rate on unanswerable questions and false-gate rate on answerable questions) wanted? It would have to be labelled a diagnostic of the retrieval gate at min_coverage=0.25, never production abstention, and it ignores the LLM stage and the short-lecture bypass.
How are short lectures handled (full-transcript bypass in production versus full_transcript_chars=0 in this baseline)?
Is a full system-level abstention evaluation (retrieval + LLM) wanted, with the LLM, prompt and temperature pinned? It needs model calls and is a later phase.

later_phases.scope: Score the evidence a production request would actually receive: qa.retrieval.select_evidence under a production-like EvidenceConfig (coverage gate, relative-score cutoff, top_k=6, context padding, merged chronological S1..Sn blocks, short-lecture full-transcript mode). The relevance rule, metrics and question sets would need their own definitions (blocks instead of chunks).

protocol_decisions.decision: Use the production-faithful "text" field; processing path documented in text_processing_path.
